decisions.outcome: agree with the small/ordinary curve policy; qualify the depth-cap edge case
decisions.why: Per-cubic device bound only tightens 0.25px and is backed by analytic curve area/perimeter and independent pixel-area tests. But depth>=16 can terminate even when flatness remains above 0.25 for very large transformed curves.
decisions.follow_up: No public visible failure established. A small geometric regression can directly measure max curve-to-polyline distance at extreme valid transforms; if it fails, determine whether document coordinates/viewport geometry can make that error visible before classifying behavior.

decisions.outcome: agree on identical-clip idempotence; qualify min-only scope and historical accuracy claims
decisions.why: Current residue/path implementation integrates exact intersection area when both sets cut a pixel and edge budgets allow; analytical 64-gon/rectangle tests verify it to half a byte. Min remains for degenerate/no-edge or bounded fallback cases and some group/clip combinations. The older claim that interval bounds establish min's relative closeness is mathematically insufficient.
decisions.follow_up: No new test needed for exact residue/path integration. Existing independent closed-form tests are strong. Potential group or fallback error remains a policy limitation absent a specified fractional output contract.

decisions.outcome: agree with shape/opacity safety and characterize min as approximate geometry
decisions.why: Current tests directly distinguish correct coincident/nested shape cases from product and use low-opacity/unknown-mask countercontrols. No current proof that min exactly integrates unrelated boundaries; group raster does not retain edges.
